subject: english-language
title: Subordinators and Complex Sentences
welcome_lead: Subordinating conjunctions let you build clever, layered sentences.
meta_desc: KS3 English Language adventure on subordinating conjunctions and complex sentences.
final_note: You can now build complex sentences using subordinators.

walkthroughs.body_html: A subordinating conjunction joins a main clause to a dependent one: 'I ran because I was late.'
The mnemonic ABCWWWWHIIT covers: After, Although, Because, Before, When, Whenever, While, Where, How, If, In case, That. Many start a subordinate clause.
A complex sentence has one main clause and at least one subordinate clause: 'Although it rained, we kept walking.'

options: By the word's grammatical function in a sentence — not its meaning. The same word can belong to different classes depending on use (e.g. 'run' as noun or verb).

mcqs.q: Are features of spoken language like 'um' and 'you know' signs of poor speech?
options: No — they are functional discourse markers and planning devices that help interaction flow, manage turn-taking and signal speaker meaning.
Fillers and false starts show the speaker is uneducated.
The IPA stands for International Phonetic Acronym.
Spoken language has no rules unlike written language.

mcqs.q: What is the IPA in linguistics?
options: Spoken language has no rules unlike written language.
The International Phonetic Alphabet — a standardised set of symbols where each symbol represents one distinct sound. Used to transcribe pronunciation precisely across all languages.
The IPA is just another alphabet like the Roman or Greek alphabet.
The IPA stands for International Phonetic Acronym.
